claims.claim: The second playthrough features repetitive puzzles and similar progression when playing as the other character.

citations.review_text: RE2 Remake is scary as hell and nails everything a survival horror game should be. The dark hallways in the police station, barely having any ammo, and Mr. X chasing you around make every second intense. The second playthrough gets a bit repetitive with the same puzzles, but it's still an 9/10 and a must-play.

Resident Evil 2 was my first Resident Evil game. I'd never really tried getting into horror games before but after hearing from a friend how good the series was, I decided to start with the remake. I had no idea what to expect and ended up enjoying it way more than I thought I would

The combat is pretty simple but I still found it really fun throughout the whole game. I never got bored of exploring and the atmosphere was definitely the highlight for me, especially inside the police station. I found it really immersive and Mr. X made some of the most memorable moments in the game. Every time I heard his footsteps I instantly started thinking about where I was going next instead of just running around without a care

I also really liked the characters. None of them feel explored that deeply but I genuinely liked all of them, especially Leon and Ada. If anything, it just made me want to keep playing the rest of the series to see where their stories go, which I think is exactly what a first game should do. The boss fights were another highlight and kept things feeling fresh throughout

I don't really have any major complaints. My only real issue is that I'm not very interested in replaying the game as Claire because while they are different characters with their own weapons, story moments and supporting characters, a lot of the overall progression is still very similar. I never played the original so I can't compare them but I do wish the two campaigns felt a bit more different from each other

Overall, I'd rate it 8/10 - Resident Evil 2 changed my opinion on horror games and made me want to play the rest of the series. Highly recommended 👮‍♂️🧟‍♂️

Resident Evil 2 Remake: Review
Score: 8/10

Resident Evil 2 Remake was the very first Resident Evil game I ever played, and what a fantastic entry point into the series—complete with some incredible highs and a few notable lows.

Powered by the then-new RE Engine, it set the blueprint for the franchise moving forward. It stands out as a pure survival horror experience where tight resource management and high-tension encounters keep you constantly on edge. Elevating the atmosphere is the iconic R.P.D. station, which remains one of the most memorable locations in the entire Resident Evil universe.

However, while the game hits all the right notes for horror, it stumbles when it comes to scenario replayability. The alternate "A/B" scenarios offer very little gameplay variety, which makes replaying them back-to-back feel repetitive rather than rewarding.

Overall, despite the disappointing lack of scenario differentiation, Resident Evil 2 Remake is a stellar title. Its masterclass in atmosphere and true survival horror gameplay keeps drawing me back into its terrifying world.

This game was my first time playing a horror game alone and also my first RE title, and god it was great, I heard that the original had more differences when it comes to Leon and Claire runs a and b, but the remake was still loads of fun, the puzzles and the exploration were great, especially the R.P.D Station where you spend most of your time, the only really lackuster part is that the runs a and b repeat themselves too much but there is still a few cool surprises to experience. There's also a few cool extra scenarios, I only finished the 4th survivor one (first try eheh) and tried the others too and I would say that those are pretty fun ! If you want to experience the full story though, you should probably do the 4th survivor extra scenario as it introduce a returning (and very well liked) character.

Performance-wise it's a capcom game so it's well optimized ( apart from DD2 and MHWA but the re engine seems to have lots of trouble with open worlds ) Despite the fact that my graphic card seems to have a few unusual problems, the was very smoothl in ultra 1440p at a fixed 120fps ( I didn't use ray tracing but when I tried it it didn't seem to change the result )

So yeah, I had a great time and I definitely intend to play the others RE titles when I have the chance.

Stream: https://youtube.com/live/9NKJpj7Z5wM?feature=share

My intention was, as part of RE:make Month I was going to finish this and then squeeze in RE3 remake, however, I had forgotten exactly how massive RE2 was (considering it has 4 playthroughs) but I had a great time with it and I over-ran into the next month, however, I kept up to make certain to get all of these stories done and out of the way!

The paths diverge quite a lot, with different weapons in the same locations:

Leon:
Starter - 9mm Pistol
Police Armoury - Shotgun
STARS Armoury - Lightning Hawk (This game's Magnum)
Sewers - Chemical Sprayer (Flame Thrower)

Claire:
Starter: .35 Pistol (Multiple ammo types with upgrade, high-power rounds can't be crafted)
Police Armoury - Grenade Launcher (Multiple ammo types. Fire and Craftable Acid rounds)
STARS Armoury - Submachinegun (Uzi essentially)
Sewers - Sparkshot (a weird weapon that fires taser-prongs and can roast an enemy with enough charge, but you need to take the time to charge)

Also, depending on if you're doing the 2nd run on Leon or the 1st on Claire, you get access to a six-shooter repeater that gets no upgrades, but fires quickly and takes it's own .44 ammo, which isn't craftable on either character. I didn't like this very much, but used it as a way to extend my resources and keep going.

Like the first remake, they managed to be fairly faithful to the main story beats and somewhat similar in the design of the police station; however, some puzzles are made different for less item-intensive ones, nor are there any statue-moving ones, which works considering Mr X could pop out of anywhere and tear you a new ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. X Gonna give it to ya, indeed!

Unlike the original, It's still either Birkin or Mr X chasing you at any given moment, whilst in the original it was either Birkin or a mutated offspring of his instead, which doesn't really appear in this one apart from in the form of rejected clumps of flesh that were dumped in …
Great game! It's pretty short, and the A/B scenarios don't differ all that much, to be honest, but the atmosphere and mechanics are great.

I liked it. I'm not usually one to replay games, so the second run was a different experience for me. Playing Claire's second run was pretty repetitive, though. There were a few changes that were interesting to see.  I probably wish I didn't spend that time - my backlog is considerable.

The thrilling and horrifying beginnings of Leon S. Kennedy and Claire Redfield. This game set the precedent for all RE remakes after it, bringing the original 1998 survival horror game into the modern gaming era.

The RPD is the centerpoint of the game, combining tight puzzle solving and tricky resource management, making you consider every bullet and grenade you use. The atmosphere and sheer dread this game manages to convey is masterful, and is told through detailed environments, satisfying gunplay and combat, and strong atmospheric lighting. 

Funnily enough my main complaint is that the RPD is so good that the game drops off a bit when you leave it. The rooms turn into long and windy mazes, the puzzles not as in-depth, and the game starts to become more and more linear as you progress. Still very enjoyable, but you've already played the best part when you finish the RPD.

Another complaint is the A and B scenarios between Leon and Claire. My take on it is when you finish your first run (whether it's Claire or Leon), you've basically played the whole game. Sure there are many differences between the 2 scenarios (mainly in the 2nd act), and it does a good job at keeping things interesting, but the game gets severely less scary because they share the same scares and the same bossfights. After playing the RE4 remake, I much preferred a singular complete story rather than playing 2 slightly different perspectives of essentially the same story. I understand they did this because it's a remake of the original, but I'm not the biggest fan of it.

Overall, this game is how a remake should be done. Taking what made the original so enjoyable and giving it not just a fresh coat of paint, but setting the foundations for the remakes that came after it. 

Looking forward to RE: Veronica and excited to see how this continues.

I played this game for the first time on Xbox Game Pass 3 years ago. It was the second RE game I played after RE4 OG. My whole perception of gaming changed after this masterpiece. I was an action-adventure-open-world-RPG gamer, but this game is a different thing from what I played. It's like a puzzle in one place, and you have to solve it. Searching for items to open more areas and going back and forth in a small place like the police station for more than 4 hours is the pure experience of this game. My mind was going to explode, asking myself how they did put all of these things in a small place like the police station, and with the inventory management-survival-scenarios-puzzles, it is something special only for this game, and it's hard to do it again after this game succeeds. The whole horror games genre is refreshed with new games like Alan Wake 2, The Calisto Protocol, and remakes like RE3, RE4, Dead Space, and Silent Hill 2. Thank you, Capcom, for this masterpiece and for what came because this game succeeded.

One of the greatest survival horror games out there. If you liked the original, you'll probably enjoy this remake as well. However it does lack the replayability in scenarios A/B, especially if you'd compare it to the original
I also recommend to play it on hardcore, even on your first playthrough. This way you'll have limited ammo and will have to leave some enemies alive and each time you'll revisit the same location you'll always have to think through the safest route or try to avoid the enemies in those tiny hallways. Limited saves will make you act more careful and won't allow you to reload from closest checkpoint, just to replay one small section you've strugled with.

The original RE2 dropped you bang middle into a furnace of chaos - from moaning zombies to burning buildings. The survival horror was truly coined into my young mind. Skip a couple of decades and RE2R drops you off in front of an abandoned gas station - before going in, I was astonished at how eerie and spooky the highway and surroundings felt. 

Once the gas station segment was done, you come to a familar iconic building - the RPD headquarters. This is where most of the claustophobic chases happen and the zombies are absolutely horrific and nightmarish. When the tyrant is released, it truly causes your heart to skip beats as if you were actually in the nightmare. 

In all, RE2R is atmospheric, gorgeous, and exhilirating. To say its my favorite Resident Evil of the series is an understatement. After getting all the achievements and S+ runs across all playthroughs, I still keep playing this masterpiece. An addictive game that balances survival horror with focused action. 

The iconic save room music is remastered and it feels nostalgic to revisit the horror from the 90s. The story is masterfully crafted, while there are a few differences between the playthroughs unlike the original which carries through your choices, it still feels fresh with Sherry and Ada introduced into specific character segements. 

I've simply run out of words to describe this game. A must play for anyone looking to experience survival horror.

The survivor mode deserves high praise. Each mini campaign showcases survivors in a "What if" scenario and it has some interesting outcomes if you make it out alive. These modes are filled with limited ammo and provide you with a pure survival style gameplay where making the wrong move means starting over again.
